methodological_rigor.justification: The review follows PRISMA, is prospectively registered on PROSPERO (CRD420251108271), uses NOS and MINORS for quality assessment, and applies a random-effects model with sensitivity analysis and publication-bias testing — all appropriate. However, meaningful methodological gaps exist: no RCTs were included (self-acknowledged), inclusion was restricted to English-only despite claiming no language restriction in the search, only 11 studies / 402 patients were pooled, and 9 of 20 full-text candidates were excluded merely because full texts were 'unavailable' (a concerning fraction suggesting possible selection bias). Statistically, 2-year and 3-year OS are reported as 'pooled' estimates despite being derived from single studies (acknowledged post hoc), several pooled rates have implausibly wide CIs (e.g., neutropenia 39% [0–86%], grade ≥3 neutropenia 38% [0–84%]) that render the estimates uninformative, publication bias was detected for CR (Egger's P=0.02), and no GRADE assessment or trim-and-fill correction is reported. Heterogeneity is very high for several core outcomes (I²=77% for CR, I²=91% for AEs) and is not fully resolved by subgroup analysis.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a systematic review and meta-analysis of predominantly non-randomized cohort/single-arm studies (4 cohort, 7 single-arm), with no RCTs — best classified as Oxford 2a. The clinical question (combination blinatumomab regimens for high-risk B-ALL including R/R and Ph+ disease) is clinically important, endpoints are patient-relevant (CR, MRD, CMR, OS), and the quantitative synthesis of CR (87%) and MRD negativity (81%) provides a useful benchmark versus monotherapy data from TOWER/BLAST. However, the absence of RCT-level evidence, high heterogeneity, and inability to compare combination vs. monotherapy directly limit guideline-changing impact; the findings reinforce rather than redirect current practice.

reporting_quality.justification: PRISMA is the correct standard and is explicitly cited; the authors report prospective PROSPERO registration, a PRISMA-style flow (Fig. 1), search strategy with databases and dates, inclusion/exclusion criteria, dual independent screening with third-reviewer adjudication, risk-of-bias assessment (NOS/MINORS), heterogeneity statistics, sensitivity analysis, and publication-bias testing. However, several PRISMA 2020 items are weak or missing: no full search string per database, no PRISMA 2020 checklist supplement cited, no explicit GRADE/certainty-of-evidence assessment, protocol deviations are not described, and justification for the English-only restriction is not provided despite claiming no language restriction. Data/code availability is essentially absent in the manuscript text — no deposition of extracted data, no analytic code shared, no explicit data-availability statement surviving the blinding.

novelty_literature.justification: The novelty is incremental: multiple prior meta-analyses of blinatumomab in B-ALL already exist and are cited in-text (Marrapodi 2022, ref. 26, on pediatric safety; Liu 2023, ref. 27, on R/R B-ALL efficacy/safety). The specific framing — combination (not monotherapy) regimens restricted to high-risk B-ALL with subgroup analyses by Ph status, treatment setting, and backbone (TKI vs. chemo) — adds a modest, targeted extension of this prior work. No new methodology, no individual-patient data pooling, no network meta-analysis, and no first-time empirical finding emerges; the subgroup contrast between TKI and chemotherapy backbones for toxicity (73% vs 99%, P=0.060) is the most interesting but not practice-defining signal.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is generally readable and well-organized along standard IMRaD/PRISMA lines, with an informative abstract and a discussion that contextualizes findings against TOWER, BLAST, ALCANTARA, E1910, and AALL1331. Problems include: several pooled estimates presented with CIs that cross zero or extend to 100% (e.g., neutropenia 39% [0–86%], 80% [28–99%] in <18 years) without explicit flagging that these are uninformative; occasional inconsistency in reported numbers (CRS incidence given as 2.1% in discussion but grade ≥3 CRS is 1.6% in results); some over-generalization in the conclusion ('potential shift in the therapeutic paradigm') that is not supported by the LoE of included studies. Figure/table captions as described in-text appear informative, and acronyms are generally defined on first use.

key_strengths: Prospective PROSPERO registration (CRD420251108271) and explicit PRISMA framing with dual-reviewer screening and quality assessment via NOS/MINORS.
Clinically meaningful question with pre-specified subgroup analyses by Ph status, treatment setting (first-line vs R/R), age, and backbone (TKI vs chemotherapy).
Appropriate random-effects model with sensitivity analyses and formal publication-bias testing (Egger's/Begg's).
Useful cross-trial benchmarking against TOWER, BLAST, ALCANTARA, E1910 and AALL1331, including a toxicity contrast suggesting chemotherapy backbone drives AE burden (99% vs 73%).
Transparent limitations section (no RCTs, single-study long-term OS estimates, residual heterogeneity, small sample sizes).
key_concerns: No RCTs included; small evidence base (11 studies, 402 patients) with 9/20 full-text eligible articles excluded as 'full text unavailable' — a non-trivial source of selection bias.

Several pooled estimates have CIs crossing zero or spanning 0–86% (e.g., neutropenia, pediatric subgroups) and are uninformative; 2- and 3-year OS presented as pooled though derived from single studies.
Very high heterogeneity (I²=77–91%) for several core outcomes, not fully resolved by subgroup analysis; publication bias detected for CR (Egger's P=0.02) with no correction attempted.
English-only inclusion despite the methods stating no language restriction in the initial search — an internal inconsistency and potential language bias.
No GRADE/certainty-of-evidence assessment, no data/code deposition, no PRISMA 2020 checklist supplement, no full per-database search strings reported.
Novelty is incremental: prior meta-analyses on blinatumomab in B-ALL (including combination/safety contexts) are already cited in the manuscript.
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a competent but incremental meta-analysis of mostly single-arm/cohort studies with methodological gaps (English-only, uninformative CIs, pooling single-study estimates, publication bias for CR) and incremental novelty against existing blinatumomab meta-analyses. It is best suited to a tier-4 oncology outlet; at that tier it would likely be acceptable with minor revisions focused on CI interpretation, GRADE assessment, data availability, and English-only justification.
